questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try studying in another European country, and I have always been fond of Italy, which is why I thought Milan would be a suitable city to study in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am overall very positive and happy about my exchange stay in Milan and I would recommend everyone to go. Unfortunately, the University, however, had some deficiencies. First and foremost, there was not the same level of assistance regarding how to navigate, how exams were conducted, or a general understanding that not everyone was from Italy. Therefore, you had to find all informations by yourself down to the smallest detail and arm oneself with patience when it came to practical matters. The university is very beautiful and you really get the feeling of being in a Harry Potter movie, but unfortunately, the exterior doesn't quite live up to the interior. It's an old university where it's very hot in the summer and super cold in the winter time. Additionally, the professors were generally not very helpful or keen on answering questions.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was very confused at the beginning of my exchange process, as Mobility Online is not very up-to-date or easy to navigate. Moreover, everything seems quite overwhelming, which is a recurring theme in all matters related to practical information in Milan. I had to research everything myself, and there wasn't much help available on the university's website. Additionally, I experienced that the staff hung up if you called and spoke English. Fortunately, I was going with some others I knew, so it helped to know that everyone was very confused, and we helped each other out. So do not worry if everything seems confusing in the beginning. The information will come and deadlines are not that important in Milan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to call and text a lot of professors and other workers at Erasmus for information, so overall I dod not get any information until I asked upon myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite challenging to find accommodation in Milan. Initially, I had planned to live alone, but it would cost around 2500-3000 euros per month. Therefore, I moved in with two other girls in an apartment, who were studying at the same university as me. We found the apartment through the company, HousingAnywhere and paid 3300 euros per month for an apartment with 3 large rooms and a spacious living room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: First of all, you can't live on campus (it is an old university). In my experience, people generally live expensively in Milan to be close to the university and the city center. Therefore, my advice is to start early in finding accommodation so you don't end up living too far away or paying too much.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the apartment we lived in, but it was expensive. There is not much help from the University, so my advice is to check Facebook groups or websites like: SpotaHome, HousingAnywhere or Airbnb. I really appreciated to live with other students although my plan had always been to live alone. But when living in a new city and studying at a new university, it is nice to have someone to come home to and do stuff with. I didn't  know the two girls I ended up living with, but we meet up before leaving for Milan and became very good friends.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As explained in the beginning, it was very difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered at Mobility Online and tried to finish all the steps I could finish with the very small information we were getting in the beginning. After that, I asked the danish Erasmus workers how to fill the steps that I needed help for. I never received help from University of Milan.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I explained this above.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to register for classes cause it was hard to find a list of the different classes. My classes overlapped, so I had to apply for entirely new classes to avoid scheduling conflicts. However, this cannot be verified when applying for credit transfer for the classes. It is important to note that you should not feel assured of obtaining all the credits applied for since they often overlap. Nevertheless, it is very easy to switch classes, and you can do this yourself midway through the semester, so there's no need to stress about it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for the classes that you find most attracting and if they overlap, then ask other students about classes that they have registered for and if they are good. You can afterwards just change classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes are interesting and Milan offer a lot of different classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level during the semester is much easier than in Copenhagen, but I found the exams challenging because the professors don't provide information on how the exams will be conducted or what is expected. The difficulty level is much lower throughout the semester, as you don't receive textbooks nor the same amount of homework. However, you have 5 courses instead of 2 or 3, so there might be more work leading up to the exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varies from professor to professor, but generally, they were a bit more distant and formal in their teaching approach. It was important to address them correctly and not be too personal in your interaction with them. Additionally, not all of them were proficient in teaching in English.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Access to Justice 
Comparative Labour Law 
Gender Justice 
Smart Cities, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation Law
Law and Policies of Social Rights Protection in Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the course: Law and Policies of Social Rights Protection in Europe

The teacher is very nice and understanding. Moreover, I liked the form of the exam. You had to do a large assignment and then talk about the assignment in the end of the course. 

Moreover, I would recommend the course: Smart Cities, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation Law

The teacher is very nice and the exam is very easy. You just have to answer some easy questions in the end of the semester about your own thoughts about the main topics.

questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend the any of the non-academic opportunities that the host institution were hosting. Therefore, I cannot comment on these. My experience is that if you know other people or students in Milan, you are good to go and its easy to make plans all the time.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside Milan and visit other cities like Verona, Bergamo or Lake Como. It is easy and cheap by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy and Italians are in general very sweet. However, many Italians dont speak English and sometimes it was hard to undertand each other.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My experience was that the local students did not attend any of the English classes. Therefore, I mostly meet other exchange students from different counties, which was also very nice. However, I had very sweet Italian neighbors, who invited us for dinner and drinks and we became good friends. Therefore, my advice is to just approach people, be open, and friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The professors are way more formal in how they approach people. Furthermore, they don't have the same culture regarding waiting times, so I often waited a very long time at places such as post offices, supermarkets, or general in public institutions. I experienced that there wasn't the same respect for other people's time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italians are very open and I liked how everyone just talked to each other on the streets and in bars and stuff.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have patience - Everything takes a long time in Milan, so don't stress about missing a deadline 

2. Look forward to live in Milan - It is an amazing experience and I will never forget my time here. 

3. Be openminded and experience as much as you can - Throughout the semester, you have a lot of time outside school hours, so just experience the city and all the beautiful places and go outside Milan for the weekend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many new people and be familiar with a new city, that I look forward to get back to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my friends and family back home. Luckily, Milan is only 2 hours away fromDenmark, so I was happy to get a lot of visitors.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
